Question about tree size...


On 3/25/14 6:34 PM, X wrote:
> Dear Nick,
>
> I'm exploring your BioGeoBEARS function in R. I'm running
> the Psychotria example and getting results. But my dataset
> is larger. First, I have 8 areas and some taxa distributed
> over the 8 areas, so I cannot even restrict the number of
> ancestral ares.
>
> numstates_from_numareas(numareas=8, maxareas=8) = 255
>
> so, it seems feasible.
>
> However, I have 230 taxa. Do you think the BioGeoBEARS can
> work with such a large dataset?
>
> If so, let me know of optimization strategies that I can
> use: tweaking min-max limits, optim vs. optimx,
> force_sparese, speedup?
>
> Thanks in advance for any tips and congrats on your work.
>
> Best,
>
> X

Hi X

BioGeoBEARS should be linear with the number of tips, so a
tree twice as big will just take twice as long. 230 taxa
should be no big deal.

speedup=TRUE and use_optimx=TRUE will help a little bit, as
would setting tighter limits on the parameters (if you can
justify doing so), but the biggest help will be using
multicore processing, e.g. setting the number of cores to 4
should be about ~4 times faster (this only applies when you
have large matrices, like you do; it will slow you down on
small matrices).

Even on an old machine, 256 states and 230 taxa should only
take a few hours at most. If you have a fast machine and 16
cores it might be a lot faster.

Cheers!
Nick
